final_candidates.decision_summary: Disrupts the N-linked glycosylation motif at N154 (N-X-T). Loss of glycosylation at this site in flaviviruses has been associated with altered replication fitness and immune evasion dynamics.
Directly removes the N-linked glycosylation acceptor at position 154. Effects on replication are context-dependent but this is a well-studied modulatory site in flavivirus envelope proteins.

history.rationale: Position 156 (T) is in the glycosylation motif at the N154 glycosylation site region; T156A may modulate glycan shielding and improve replication efficiency in certain cell types by balancing immune evasion with receptor accessibility.

T156 is part of the N-linked glycosylation motif at position 154 (N-X-T). Removing glycosylation at N154 via T156A can enhance viral replication in certain cell types by altering immune evasion and receptor binding dynamics.
Position 107 (L) is in the hydrophobic core of domain II; phenylalanine may strengthen hydrophobic packing and stabilize the prefusion trimer, enhancing particle assembly.
L107F is a conservative hydrophobic substitution in domain II that may subtly alter domain interactions or fusion loop accessibility without disrupting fold.

N154 is the well-characterized glycosylation site on Zika E protein; removing this glycan has been shown in related flaviviruses to alter tropism and replication kinetics, potentially enhancing fitness in specific host environments.
N154 is the glycosylation site itself; its removal has been shown in flaviviruses to affect viral fitness, though effects are context-dependent and sometimes detrimental.
